tagline.text: An outlet and leisure complex on a former textile mill site by the Marikina River

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,500 (per person for a half day, including transport, food and light shopping)

children.text: Riverbanks Center is a shopping and leisure complex that opened in 1999 on about 23 hectares beside the Marikina River. Outlet stores, a riverside park and a large open-air venue sit side by side, and the place gets busy with Christmas events from mid-October.

Riverbanks Center is a mixed-use shopping, leisure and business complex in Barangay Barangka, Marikina, in eastern Metro Manila, right beside the Marikina River. The address is 84 Andres Bonifacio Avenue, and the site covers about
23 hectares
. Locals often just call it "Riverbanks."

The land was once the Universal Textile Mills (UTEX) factory, described as one of the largest textile mills in Asia. After the mill stopped operating around 1994, Riverbanks Development Corporation bought the site and opened the complex in
April 1999
; it is presented as Marikina's first shopping mall. Unlike a typical mall, the old factory atmosphere remains, with many low, single-story buildings spread out over a wide area.

There are three main attractions: outlet stores selling branded goods at a discount, a broad grassy area that meets the Marikina River Park, and the Riverbanks Amphitheater, an open-air venue said to hold up to 20,000 people. A roller skating rink, a convention center and food areas add to the mix. The complex also houses the Philippine Science Centrum, an NBI satellite office and Queen of Angels Chapel, so it is not only about shopping.

That said, this is less a headline Philippine tourist attraction than an everyday complex that Marikina residents visit for shopping, strolls and events. A recent visitor's account notes that some shops closed during the pandemic and some areas feel quiet, so keep expectations modest and treat it as one stop in a Marikina day. On the other hand, if you avoid rainy days and time your visit to an event, you will enjoy it much more. It is a distance from central Manila, so allow plenty of time for the trip.

Riverbanks is described as having the largest outlet store in the Philippines, and brands such as Adidas, Nike, Puma, Levi's and Converse have been tenants in the past. Visitors report clearance items and overstock clothing and furniture from other retailers. Tenants change often, so check the official social media pages before you go.
The back of the complex meets the Marikina River Park, which stretches about
11 km
along the river. It is a pleasant place for walking or cycling, and Marikina is known as a bike-friendly city. The riverside can flood after heavy rain.
This open-air venue on the sloping ground between the mall and the river holds up to
20,000 people
. Records show a major celebrity concert there in December 2024. Some sources, however, say it is closed because of a river improvement project, so reports conflict. Confirm locally before you go.

This is the complex's signature event, held from mid-October into January or February. It combines a carnival with rides and games, a bazaar selling crafts and gifts, food booths and stage shows. The 2024–2025 edition was listed as running
October 15–January 15
; no 2026 schedule has been confirmed.
Visitors mention a roller skating rink, a rarity among modern malls. Operating hours and fees could not be confirmed, so ask on site. It is worth adding to a half-day plan if you have children.

Most buildings are single-story former factory structures, so you can walk around without going up and down floors. Large parking areas and outdoor food spaces make it comfortable for families. Quiet hours are also good for taking photos.

blocks.title: Outdoor food spaces and fast food

children.text: The complex is said to have standalone fast-food outlets, an outdoor food park and a supermarket. During the Christmas events, food booths multiply, from Filipino dishes to international cuisine. Prices vary by outlet, so check on site.
Arrive at Riverbanks Center by taxi or jeepney. The mall's opening hours could not be officially confirmed, so arriving in the late morning is safer.
Walk around the outlet stores. The single-story buildings are easy to walk, and you should check size and condition yourself before buying.
Have lunch at a fast-food outlet or the outdoor food area in the complex.
Head to the riverbank behind the mall and walk the Marikina River Park, or find out whether you can rent a bicycle.
Look around the amphitheater area and the monuments, then head home before dark. If the weather turns cloudy, wrap up the riverside early.
If you also want to see Marikina's shoe heritage, you can follow up the same day with shoe-related sights in central Marikina.
Arrive when the carnival opens. In the 2024 edition, the carnival started around 4 p.m.
Browse crafts and gifts at the bazaar and have dinner at the food booths.
Watch a stage show or take the children on the rides.
Book a taxi or ride-hailing car in advance and leave before the crowds peak. Roads can be congested on event evenings.

items.title: From Manila by LRT-2 and a transfer

children.text: One suggested route is to take LRT-2 from central Manila (Legarda, Recto and so on) to Katipunan station and transfer to a jeepney. As of a March 2026 report, LRT-2 fares carry a 50% DOTr discount (single-journey tickets ₱8–18), and Legarda or Recto to Katipunan or Santolan is about
and the jeepney at about
(the jeepney figure is from old data), but fares may change when the discount ends or fares are revised, so check locally.
Santolan station on LRT-2 is known as the nearest train station, and the walk from there to the complex is about
2 km
(about
26 minutes
). A tricycle or jeepney is better than walking.
Routes and transfers can change, so check the latest route on a map app.
Travel time from Manila depends heavily on traffic, so an exact figure is hard to give.

items.title: From Manila by taxi or ride-hailing

children.text: From central Manila or Makati, a taxi or ride-hailing car is the easiest option. Enter 84 Andres Bonifacio Avenue or "Riverbanks Center" as the destination.
Avoid weekday morning and evening rush hours, when Marcos Highway and the C-5 area are congested.
Jeepneys, tricycles and buses serve the complex, and Riverbanks Avenue links to Marcos Highway and C-5 Road.
The Riverbanks Transport Terminal and the Metro Manila Eastern Transport Hub are near the complex.
From within Marikina, you can also take a Marikina–Pasig tricycle to Riverbanks.

Riverbanks is liveliest from mid-October, when the ChristmasSaya events start, through January or February. The carnival, bazaar and shows continue, and a year-end concert and fireworks display on December 30 is reported. A national fireworks festival on Saturdays in April is also mentioned, but check whether it is held this year.

The riverside can flood in the rainy season. Records show the whole complex was under water during Typhoon Ondoy in 2009 and Typhoon Ulysses in 2020. It is best to avoid visiting when a typhoon is approaching.
Marikina is mostly flat and easy to walk, but the midday sun is strong. Plan outdoor time for the morning or around sunset.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Christmas events and year-end fireworks; busiest period
Go outdoors early in the morning or in the evening; check the schedule for the April fireworks event
Flood and typhoon risk; stick to the indoor outlets

items.label: Admission
items.note: Entering the complex is reported to be free, but there is no recent official confirmation. Rides and parking during events cost extra (2014 data: rides ₱30–40, parking ₱45)

A lodging called Courtyard Dormtel is said to be on the grounds, but its current status and rates could not be confirmed. If you need a place to stay, compare options near SM City Marikina and Ayala Malls Marikina, or in Quezon City and Pasig.

For meals, you can use the standalone fast-food outlets, the outdoor food park and the supermarket in the complex. During the Christmas events, food booths ranging from traditional Filipino dishes to international cuisine greatly widen your choices. Central Marikina has more variety.

The riverside breeze can be pleasant in the evening, but on weekdays without events some shops may close early. Do not leave dinner too late, and plan your ending around the last available transport. If you are not used to Filipino food, fast-food outlets are a safe choice.
Check the official Facebook or Instagram pages of Riverbanks Center for events and hours before you go. The official website showed a maintenance page when we checked.
For outlet goods, check condition, size and stitching yourself, and keep the receipt.
During events, weekend evenings are crowded, so aim for a weekday afternoon or arrange your transport in advance.
The sun is strong at the riverside park, so bring a hat, water and sunscreen.
If you want to cycle, ask locally about bicycle rental in Marikina. Whether rentals are available inside the complex could not be confirmed.
Combine it with the shoe-related sights in central Marikina for a fuller day.
If rain is forecast, skip the riverside walk and plan around the indoor outlets.
If you travel in a group, you can split up for the outlets and meet for the riverside walk to use your time well.
The site is close to the river and can flood during typhoons and heavy rain. Do not visit in bad weather.
Some sources say the amphitheater is closed because of a river improvement project, while another record reports a concert in December 2024. Confirm availability locally.
After the 2020 flood, the Shoe Gallery in the complex was permanently closed and the giant shoes were removed. Do not go looking for it based on old guides.
Visitors report closed shops and empty office space since the pandemic, so some areas can feel quiet.
If you head home late in the evening, use a ride-hailing car and watch your belongings.
Tenants and opening hours change often, so check the latest announcements.
Central Marikina is close to Riverbanks, so it is easy to combine in one day. You can see the history of the shoe industry and shoe shops together.
A riverside park about
11 km
long that touches the complex, with walking paths, bike routes and a skating rink.
A large nearby mall that opened in 2008. You can compare it with Riverbanks.
A pilgrimage and viewpoint city in Rizal province, east of Marikina. If you go on the same day, allow plenty of time for travel.
